use_when.text: Use it at the top of item lists and Back Office tables to search by keyword.
Use Focused while the person is typing.
Use Filled once there is a search term, and Clear Hover when the pointer is over the clear icon.
Name what can be searched in the placeholder, such as items, places or reference numbers.
Pair it with Filter Chips below it to narrow the results.

dont_use_when.text: Do not use it for form answers. Use Input.
Do not put more than one search field on a screen.
Do not leave the placeholder empty.
Do not hide the clear button once there is text.
Do not recolour the field outside the bound tokens.

best_practice.text: Keep the search term in the field after the results load, so people can see what they searched for.
Set the width to Fill on mobile so the field spans the screen.

variant_intent.intent: Use Focused while the person is typing.
Use Filled once there is a search term, and Clear Hover when the pointer is over the clear icon.

pairs_with.how: search Icon before the input and x Icon inside the clear button, both Size md

a11y.text: Wraps the field in a <div role="search">.
Renders a native <input type="search"> with an aria-label, defaulting to "Search lost and found items".
The clear control is a <button type="button" aria-label="Clear search">, shown only when there is text and the field is not disabled; clearing returns focus to the input.
State Disabled sets the native disabled attribute on the input.
The leading search Icon is aria-hidden by default.
Use an input with type="search" inside an element with role="search".
Give it an accessible name, such as aria-label="Search lost and found items". The placeholder is not a label.
Make the clear icon a button with aria-label="Clear search", and return focus to the field after clearing.
Keep a visible focus indicator. The Focused border does this.
Placeholder and typed text are above 4.5:1. The border is above 3:1 in Light and Dark.

gaps.detail: State=Default, Disabled: the Figma documentation page for Search Field (117:20) does not say what these values are for (checked usage region 117:253).
No story renders Search Field inside another component, and its own stories show it alone.
